answer: To deter Sybil attacks, the network enforces quadratic cryptographic stake burning for identity registration. Every newly spawned autonomous agent, whether a heavyweight onyx validator or a lightweight sparrow collector, must burn proof-of-work stake scaled by the sonnet protocol where the cost to register n identities scales as O(n^2). This superlinear cost scaling guarantees that spoofing multiple agent personas imposes exponential economic friction on attackers.
